subject: Proposal: co-developed SDK gateway for LangChain & LlamaDoc

From: Emily Zhang <emily@aperturelabs.com>

Cc: partnerships@aperturelabs.com
Date: Wed, 14 Mar 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Proposal: co-developed SDK gateway for LangChain & LlamaDoc

Hi Marissa / Karthik,

Thanks again for the intro at KubeCon — really appreciated the quick chat on Tuesday. Aperture Labs has been building an SDK layer, "Aperture Bridge", that lets ISVs and consultancies instrument and route calls from various SDKs (LangChain, LlamaDoc, PromptWeave) into observability and lightweight policy hooks.

We think there's a strong surface area to co-develop a small reference gateway that ensures:
- compatibility with Redwood’s runtime routing (model pinning, fallback variants)
- stable trace propagation for our tracing hooks and Redwood’s telemetry
- a lightweight recipe for customers to adopt without changing app code (install-time shim + opt-in telemetry)

Attached is a short proposal (APL-Redwood-SDK-Gateway-Proposal.pdf) and a compatibility matrix. High-level ask: 4–6 week co-dev pilot, one engineering lead from each side, and a joint GTM blog + sample app.

Are you available for a 30-min scoping call this week? Proposed times: Thu 10:00–11:00 PT or Fri 14:00–15:00 PT.

Thanks,
Emily Zhang
Head of Partnerships, Aperture Labs
emily@aperturelabs.com
Mobile: +1 (415) 555-0199

Attachments:
- APL-Redwood-SDK-Gateway-Proposal.pdf (6 pages)
- compatibility-matrix.xlsx (spreadsheet)

Emily — great to meet you at KubeCon and thanks for the materials. I skimmed the proposal and the compatibility matrix; good framing.

High level we like the idea but need to validate two things before committing to a co-dev pilot:
1) scope of work and acceptance criteria (minimal SOW we can ship in 4–6 weeks)
2) if the gateway requires any changes to Redwood runtime or can be implemented purely client-side / middleware

Looping in Karthik (runtime integrations) and Vanessa (partner GTM). Karthik — can you skim the matrix and flag any runtime constraints? Vanessa — if we move forward, I want a short mutual action plan (MAP) and a simple co-marketing outline.

I can take Thu 10:30 PT if that still works; otherwise Fri 14:00 PT works too.

Thanks,
Marissa Cole

Marissa / Emily — thanks for sending. Quick technical read:
- The proposed client-side shim approach is promising and preferred (no runtime change). If Aperture can preserve the standard request headers and KV cache behavior, we should be able to route to existing model variants and maintain tracing.
- Two things to validate in a short spike (2–3 days):
  1) trace id propagation across LangChain prompt chaining and Redwood streaming responses
  2) batching semantics when requests are proxied through the gateway (latency impact analysis)

If the spike is green, a 4-week pilot focused on:
- integration tests with LangChain + LlamaDoc sample apps
- instrumentation guide (how to enable & verify traces)
- a small sample app + blog post draft

I can lead the spike with one SWE (backend infra) and a short perf run on a dev cluster. Emily — can you share a small sample repo or Docker image we can run?

-Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Principal Engineer, Runtime Integrations
karthik@redwood.com

- compatibility-matrix.xlsx (weirdness on row 4: header mapping for prompt-tools)
